🇲🇽🏥 <u>MEXICO IS ON TRACK FOR THE HIGHEST MEDICAL INFLATION IN THE WORLD IN 2026</u>

Private medical costs in Mexico are projected to rise 14.8% in 2026 — the steepest of any country on earth, per Aon's global report cited by El Economista — while general inflation runs near 3.2%. INEGI already measured health-service inflation at 4.83% in June against 3.37% overall, with outpatient care jumping 8.81%. Private medicine is now the most inflationary sector in the country.

🇲🇽📜 <u>THE CÓDICE AZCATITLAN IS IN MEXICO CITY FOR THE FIRST TIME — LOANED BACK BY FRANCE</u>

The Códice Azcatitlan — a 20-page pictographic manuscript tracing the Mexica migration from Aztlán to the founding of Mexico-Tenochtitlan — went on display September 18 at the National Museum of Anthropology, loaned by France to mark 200 years of bilateral ties after Presidents Sheinbaum and Macron negotiated the deal. Mexico sent the Códice Boturini to Paris in exchange, and admission is free through December 6.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>SHEINBAUM SNUBS PAN GOVERNOR'S BACKROOM MEETING AMID PROBE OF A CIA OPERATION IN CHIHUAHUA</u>

In Ciudad Juárez, President Sheinbaum declined a private working meeting sought by Chihuahua's PAN governor Maru Campos — sending Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez in her place — with a blunt "I'm really going to the event and then I'm leaving for Baja California." The chill is substantive: the federal government and the state are at odds over a probe, now before the FGR, into the participation of CIA agents in an operation on Chihuahua soil, and Campos wanted to reopen talks on the 1944 water treaty with Washington.
banner: SHEINBAUM SNUBS PAN GOV OVER CIA PROBE

text:
🚨🇲🇽 <u>THE EMPIRE NOW LECTURING MEXICO ON "SOVEREIGNTY" ONCE INVADED VERACRUZ FOR ITS OIL</u>

Washington lectures Mexico today about "corrupt officials" and interference. In April 1914 it landed more than 6,000 troops in Veracruz on a manufactured pretext — the "Tampico affair" — after already engineering the coup and murder of President Madero through Ambassador Henry Lane Wilson. The target was Mexico's oil and railways; Admiral Fletcher himself counted 193 Mexican dead, and civilians — women hauling ammunition and tending the wounded among them — held the port for seven months until the invaders finally withdrew.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S BIGGEST-EVER FUEL-THEFT BUST SAT ON PERMITS SIGNED BY THE PAN AND THE GREEN PARTY</u>

The 59 million liters of stolen fuel the FGR seized in San José Iturbide, Guanajuato — the largest huachicol bust in Mexican history — sat in a terminal that grew under PRI, PAN and Green Party (PVEM) governments. Gas Natural del Noroeste was inaugurated in 2017 under Peña Nieto with a PAN governor present; a PAN mayor first authorized the site in 2012, and a PVEM-led council later approved the ownership change and its expansion to 100-million-liter capacity.
banner: RECORD FUEL BUST ON PAN & GREEN PERMITS

🇲🇽🏭 <u>US CARMAKERS LOBBY TRUMP TO WALL CHINESE AUTOS OUT OF NORTH AMERICA</u>

GM, Ford, Toyota, VW, Stellantis, Hyundai and Tesla signed a joint letter urging Trump to keep "the door firmly closed to Chinese automobile manufacturers that intend to sell, import or manufacture vehicles" in North America — days before his meeting with Xi. Their real worry is south of the border: BYD and other Chinese brands are now common on Mexican roads, and Detroit is lobbying Washington to force them out of the T-MEC market.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICAN INDUSTRY POSTS ITS BEST GROWTH IN 3 YEARS</u>

Mexico's industrial output rose 2.42% year-on-year in July — its strongest reading in 33 months, according to INEGI — driven by a 6.66% jump in construction and manufacturing returning to growth (+1.33%) after 12 straight months of contraction. Manufacturing of computer and electronic equipment surged 13.5%, its best in 43 months.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>PUEBLA'S MOBILE HOSPITAL BRINGS FREE SURGERY TO THE POOR</u>

Puebla's new "5 de Mayo" itinerant hospital travels to isolated communities performing cataract, pterygium, hernia and other surgeries at no cost — its 210 m² operating room, filtering 99.97% of bacteria, is billed as the largest in Latin America. Governor Alejandro Armenta opened it as healthcare that goes to the people; one patient from Teziutlán, after cataract surgery: "they made our dream to see again come true." A second mobile hospital is already budgeted for next year.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PRI'S BOSS LOCKS IN POWER TO 2032</u>

Alejandro "Alito" Moreno rewrote the PRI's statutes to allow indefinite reelection, securing his grip on the party — and its roughly 800 million pesos a year in public financing from the INE — until 2032, all while under multiple corruption probes. In August 2026 two of his associates were arrested over an alleged 36-million-peso diversion via fake invoices. This is the man caught on tape saying journalists shouldn't be shot — "you have to starve them to death."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>FOBAPROA'S ARCHITECT STILL CASHES A LIFETIME CHECK</u>

Ernesto Zedillo — the president who in 1997 turned private bankers' losses into public debt through Fobaproa — still draws a 149,203-peso monthly lifetime pension from Banxico (about 1.8 million a year), even after AMLO scrapped ex-presidents' pensions. Finance Secretary Edgar Amador: "we've paid nearly 1.6 trillion pesos over the years and not a single peso of principal has been paid." The bailout's net liabilities still stood at 1.01 trillion pesos in June 2026.
